{{Quote|Duracrete slug. About ten meters long, by the look of him. They burrow into the stone. Best to keep an eye out.|[[Keets Freely]] to [[Trever Flume]]|<ref name="The Last of the Jedi: Underworld">''[[The Last of the Jedi: Underworld]]''</ref>}}
Having been spread throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] by [[Freighter/Legends|freighters]] and cargo ships, '''duracrete slugs''' were large [[Silica parasite/Legends|silica parasite]] [[Mollusk/Legends|mollusks]] that dug tunnels into building foundations and fed off the [[Duracrete/Legends|duracrete]] therein, using their [[Mouth/Legends|mouths]] powerful muscles. This was then excreted on to the skin, forming [[Armor/Legends|armor]]. They also possessed nodules on their armored skin, formed from the excreted elements of indigestible [[Concrete/Legends|concrete]]. Duracrete slugs were virtually blind, but had feelers capable of sensing rock layers. While their average length was three to five [[Meter/Legends|meters]], some specimens on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] were known to reach ten meters in length, especially in the [[Coruscant Underworld/Legends|Coruscant underlevels]]. While extremely similar in appearance to the [[Duracrete worm|duracrete worm]], the duracrete slug possessed distinctive nodule ridges on its back.<ref name="Ep 2 Dictionary" />

==Behind the scenes==
The species was created by concept sculptor [[Robert E. Barnes]] in collaboration with author [[David West Reynolds]] for the reference book [[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]].<ref name="Archive">{{SWArchive|url=eu/lit/ref/f20061031/index.html|text=Building a ''Complete Visual Dictionary''}}</ref>

According to Robert E. Barnes the duracrete slug is a "species-shift" from the [[duracrete worm]] in the [[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]] book by [[Terryl Whitlatch]]. With the main difference between the two being the soft and slimy skin of the duracrete worm while the duracrete slug has armored skin developed from consuming and excreting duracrete.<ref name="Archive" />
